definition: In natural language processing a w-shingling is a set of unique shingles (therefore n-grams) each of which is composed of contiguous subsequences of tokens within a document, which can then be used to ascertain the similarity between documents.
details: The symbol w denotes the quantity of tokens in each shingle selected, or solved for. The document, "a rose is a rose is a rose" can therefore be maximally tokenized as follows: (a,rose,is,a,rose,is,a,rose) The set of all contiguous sequences of 4 tokens (Thus 4=n, thus 4-grams) is { (a,rose,is,a), (rose,is,a,rose), (is,a,rose,is), (a,rose,is,a), (rose,is,a,rose) } Which can then be reduced, or maximally shingled in this particular instance to { (a,rose,is,a), (rose,is,a,rose), (is,a,rose,is) }.

explainer.lead: W-shingling represents a document as the set of unique shingles, each a contiguous subsequence of w tokens. It is used to ascertain similarity between documents.

tiers.eli5: You cut a sentence into overlapping word chunks and keep each distinct chunk once, then compare chunk sets to see how alike two texts are.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it for document similarity by building shingle sets and comparing them. A pitfall is that much depends on the chosen shingle width w and on tokenization.
tiers.paperLevel: For a document tokenized into tokens, the set of unique contiguous subsequences of w tokens; the symbol w denotes the quantity of tokens in each shingle.

explainer.example: For "a rose is a rose is a rose", all contiguous 4-token sequences reduce to the set {(a,rose,is,a), (rose,is,a,rose), (is,a,rose,is)}.
